# Account Settings and Portal

Your account console is the central hub for configuring your organization and managing your team. From here you can control branding, display defaults, invoice content, email behavior, webhooks, payment settings, members, and organization details.

## Branding

Upload a PNG or JPG logo and add a short caption to personalize your document
previews and customer-facing output. You can replace or remove your logo at any
time from the Branding page.

It's worth previewing your final document output after making changes — your logo and caption may appear differently depending on the export format.

## Display Defaults

Display Options let you set defaults for how new estimates, invoices, and work views are presented. There are two groups of settings here:

- **Invoice display defaults** — control room pricing, line item pricing, list-style item display, and coat labels.
- **Work display defaults** — control whether line, room, section, or project time appears on work output.

These defaults apply to new or newly rendered work. Changing them won't retroactively update existing projects.

## Invoice Content

Invoice Content is where you manage reusable project note templates and your invoice disclaimer text. Note templates help you standardize the language that gets added to new projects, and the disclaimer appears below customer document content.

Because estimates and invoices can share page behavior, preview your output after editing to make sure your wording lands the way you expect.

## Messaging

Messaging settings give you control over three things: which project emails are copied to your internal inbox, customer reply addresses, and the introductory text on estimate and invoice emails.

Internal copy lists are validated before saving, so you'll know right away if an address is malformed. For reply routing, you can either use a shared support address or let replies go back to the project creator.

Pick which project emails get copied internally: estimates, invoices, sold work orders, payment requests, and payment receipts. If you've never saved a selection, EstimateSync keeps copying estimates, invoices, and work orders until you save one.

When a project is sold, the work-order email goes to your internal copy list as long as work orders are selected. Unselect work orders — or leave the list empty — and the sold work order goes to the project creator instead.

Estimate and invoice emails are sent to the internal copy list when those types are selected. When sending one, you can add CC recipients for that email from the confirmation screen. See the projects guide for details.

You can also update your introductions while sending: owners and admins who edit an estimate or invoice email introduction can save it as the new default for future emails.

## Webhooks

Webhooks connect EstimateSync with a CRM, form service, spreadsheet, or
automation tool. Use the console to copy the inbound contact and sold-project
endpoints, manage their secret keys, or choose where EstimateSync sends
outbound project events.

The [Integrations guide](/docs/guide/integrations) explains the request headers,
JSON bodies, responses, outbound event data, and webhook signature checks.

## Payments

Payment Settings define your organization-level defaults for payment requests. You can configure:

- Email receipt behavior
- Default deposit
- Cash and check instructions
- Payment links

A default deposit is a fixed amount or a percentage of the invoice total. When a project is sold for the first time, EstimateSync fills it into the send prompt, requests it in the invoice email, and tracks it as a deposit on the project's balance. You can change or clear the deposit on any later sale until the client has paid it. The amount is capped at the invoice balance. Leave it blank if you don't collect deposits.

Payment links must use HTTPS URLs. They open outside of EstimateSync, so treat them as external destinations you're pointing your customers to.

## Members and Organization

Members and Organization controls live in the account console, but the details — roles, invites, ownership transfer, leaving, and rejoining — are covered in the team access guide.
